cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Your Turn
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept responsibility for a task you believe should never have been yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I took your bins out once during your holiday. I didn't volunteer for life. Tonight's yours. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbours already send you the reminders.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'll introduce you in the group as their permanent bin contact.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stay in it until I know what I'm doing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll stay until you send 'I'll handle Thursday.' They can welcome you while I leave.

mechanism: A directs a bin-duty handover but accepts a supporting role to make B publicly own the task A only covered temporarily.
confusable: Unlike shared chore planning, A explicitly rejects a permanent job that began as a favor; confident control survives by conceding handover support.
comparison: Neighbor group and written public ownership differ from physical mop transfer and training.
seedUse: Use canonical D29-b holiday cover and reminder group, with S02-a taking credit for an adjustment B actually requests.
